key_insight: FineCog-Nav organizes zero-shot UAV vision-language navigation as a top-down cognitive stack of fine-grained modules (language, perception, reasoning, control), enabling better coordination and compositional generalization without heavy retraining of large base models.
problem_solved: Enables reliable zero-shot, long-horizon egocentric UAV navigation from ambiguous, multi-step language instructions by replacing loosely coupled monolithic pipelines with tightly specified, interoperable cognitive modules.
method: Top-down cognitive framework that decomposes VLN into specialized modules (fine-grained language parser, scene-perception, task reasoner, and motion controller) with explicit interfaces.

Cross-module coordination using lightweight communication protocols (e.g., structured semantic tokens and attention-based message passing) to compose capabilities zero-shot from pre-trained multimodal backbones.
Modular adapters and planners that translate high-level instructions into stepwise subgoals and robust low-level control commands suitable for egocentric UAV execution.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building composable, interpretable zero-shot multimodal agents for UAVs and other embodied platforms, reducing dependence on huge end-to-end retraining and improving generalization to new environments and instructions.

paper_title: FineCog-Nav: Integrating Fine-grained Cognitive Modules for Zero-shot Multimodal UAV Navigation
paper_authors: Dian Shao, Zhengzheng Xu, Peiyang Wang, Like Liu, Yule Wang
